modules.name: uart_tx_core
modules.behavior: UART 8N1 transmitter with a valid/ready byte input, public parameter DIV=868 (clock cycles per bit; 868 gives 115200 baud from a 100 MHz clock). Supported experiment domain: integer DIV 2..4096. Preserve the parameter and its effect on timing, not only the default. Ports: in_data[7:0], in_valid, in_ready (output), tx (output, the serial line). Idle: tx=1 and in_ready=1. A byte is accepted at rising edge k when in_valid && in_ready && !rst; in_data is captured at that edge and later input changes are ignored until the frame ends. The frame is 10 bits, each exactly DIV cycles long, least significant data bit first: bit 0 is the start bit (0), bits 1..8 are in_data[0]..in_data[7], bit 9 is the stop bit (1). Bit i is visible on tx after the NBA update of edge k+i*DIV and stays until the NBA update of edge k+(i+1)*DIV. in_ready is 0 after edge k and becomes 1 again after the NBA update of edge k+10*DIV, when the transmitter is idle again with tx=1; the earliest next accept is edge k+10*DIV+1, so back-to-back frames are separated by a stop level of DIV+1 cycles. in_valid while busy is ignored, not queued. tx and in_ready are registered outputs: they change only at rising edges, never combinationally from inputs or from rst. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge aborts any frame and returns to idle (tx=1, in_ready=1) and overrides an accept at the same edge; it has no effect between edges. For the Python golden model, each non-reset step is one clock edge with that step's inputs, returning tx and in_ready after the edge.
